resources.string: A quiet pause before distracting apps
Momentwise doesn\'t block apps or lock you out. It gives you a calm moment to ask why you tapped an app, and gentle reminders so you don\'t lose an hour by accident.
Choose your apps: Pick which apps pause when opened.
Customise your prompt: Write your own question and response options.
Respectful reminders: Set how often to check in, or turn them off completely.
Choose an app to guard. That is the next step.
Monitoring is on. A pause can cover a guarded app. It may be about a second late.
Monitoring is on. Without display over other apps, Momentwise cannot cover the other app. You will get a notification to tap. The other app is not blocked until you open it.
A rule is saved, but monitoring is off until Usage Access and notifications are allowed.
Monitoring is not running. The ongoing notification is gone, so opening a selected app will not show a pause until it starts again.

The ongoing notification is not running. Saved rules are still here. Start monitoring again from this screen. A phone battery manager can stop it after you leave Momentwise; this app cannot override that, and it will not keep relaunching itself.

Leave goes home. It does not force-stop the other app. A trip away under a minute, without Leave, keeps the same visit. Reminders count time in the app, not time away, and can be about 15 seconds late.
A check-in was in progress before the phone restarted. That session was dropped. The next time a guarded app opens, the pause starts again.
Looks only. A preview does not start a session or a timer.
Enable an app: Pick distracting social or news apps in the Apps tab.
Set your prompt: Write a question that makes you pause before opening.
Check in gracefully: If you stay in the app, a gentle nudge helps you leave.
These are apps you can open on this device. Each rule is stored only here. This list is not a usage report.
The earlier sample apps were removed. Their settings were not copied onto real apps. Choose the apps installed on this device.
Each app has its own independent rule, opening prompt, and reminder schedule. Enabling one asks for access only after you read why.
Shown under the question when this app opens.
Give yourself two clear choices when the notice appears.
Returns to the home screen. Does not force-stop the other app.
Stays in the app and starts the saved reminder, if there is one.
Choose how often Momentwise checks in while you stay in this app.
Appears on the check-in card when the time expires.
No reminders will be scheduled while in this app. The opening notice will still pause when launched.
Personalise what happens when a reminder appears.
Dismissing pauses further reminders for this app until tomorrow. It does not permanently disable your rule.
Returns you to the home screen. Does not force-stop the other app.
Preview. This does not start a live session or cover another app.
In-app preview. It does not start a live reminder.
Choose between System, Light, or Dark mode. System follows your device setting.
Leave returns to the home screen. Momentwise does not force-stop the other app.
Rules stay on this phone. Monitoring runs only while a rule is enabled and access is allowed.
Clear saved rules and any in-progress check-in on this device.
This clears saved rules and any in-progress check-in stored on this device. It does not change other apps.
You paused and chose not to open %1$s. In the native app this returns you to your home screen. It does not force-stop the other app.
Preview only. Continuing into %1$s would start a check-in after %2$d minutes of use. This preview does not start one.
Continuing into %1$s. No mid-session reminders are scheduled.
You configured %1$s with reminder frequency Never. Only the opening notice pauses when the app is launched.
Check-in after %1$d minutes of use in %2$s
Exit action: in the native app this returns you to your home screen.
Continue action: the app would open normally.
Reminders paused for %1$s for the rest of today.
Saved rules stay as they are. While this is on, Momentwise does not watch for guarded apps or show a pause.
Read from Android, not from a button tap. The control says Allow until Android reports the grant, then Allowed. Opening Settings does not grant access by itself.
Not allowed — a notification will be used instead
Pause %1$s only if you want Momentwise to notice it

Momentwise does not force-stop the app or lock you out. If you allow display over other apps, a pause covers it until you choose. Otherwise it cannot cover the app. You can decline and keep editing rules.

Used only to see which app is in the foreground, on this phone, so your pause can appear. It is not used to read messages, build a usage dashboard, or send anything off the device. Android asks for this in Settings, not in a normal permission dialog.
Optional. A card can cover the middle of the screen. If you skip this, Momentwise uses a notification instead and does not block the other app.

A quiet ongoing status while monitoring is active, with a Pause action to stop it. If Momentwise cannot cover another app, it may show a separate notification you can tap. That notification does not block the app. No streaks, no marketing.
The pause can be about a second late. Leave goes to the home screen and does not force-stop the other app.
Usage Access and notifications are still needed
A quiet status while your selected app pauses are active. Use Pause monitoring to stop it.
A notification you can open when the pause could not cover the other app. It does not block that app.
Quietly checking the apps you selected.
The app is not blocked. This is a notification, not a cover over %1$s. Open it to choose.
Opened from a notification. The other app was not covered until you opened this.
Momentwise pause over %1$s. The app behind is not available until you choose.
Leave returns you to the home screen. It does not force-stop the other app, stop its audio, or clear its back stack.
Snooze this prompt and check again later.
You\'ve been here for a while.
A small pause can help you feel more in control of your time.
